findings.actual_security_impact: The caller can read any regular file allowed by its OS permissions, up to the configured bound. This is a real capability. If a more-privileged agent or server accepted untrusted path choices, the same helper could cross that caller authorization boundary and disclose data.
findings.fix_or_safe_use_rationale: Exact-head flow is argparse.parse_args at line 301 -> args.build -> read_source at line 49 -> os.open at line 51. The Sonar flow labels parse_args as an HTTP source; the inspected code is a standalone local CLI, with no in-repo HTTP/agent caller. The operator explicitly supplies --build; capture fields do not select paths. No process privilege elevation or shell interpolation occurs. No-follow/nonblocking regular-file checks and bounded reads prevent symlink/FIFO and resource hazards, but are not a path allowlist. The complete build manifest must equal the pinned manifest before claims. Reuse with untrusted agent/server arguments requires an independently authorized input-root/capability policy and is unsupported here. Leave the HIGH finding OPEN for independent review; do not treat those file flags as a general traversal fix.

findings.actual_security_impact: Container UID 0 has elevated access within the build container. A privileged/rootful invocation or broad writable host mount would be unsafe.
findings.fix_or_safe_use_rationale: Supported invocation is rootless Podman, pinned image/packages, read-only producer mount, scratch-only write mounts, network disabled while compiling, and no deployed service. Do not interpret this as approval for privileged/rootful deployment.
